clue.text: Villain caught associate surrounded by proceeds of robbery

indicators.note: the pieces for caught and associate sit with the loot wrapped round them

parts.note: swag is slang for stolen goods
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.surface: A crook, his accomplice and the stolen goods are found together by police.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal or rogue is a lighthearted name for a villain or troublemaker.

clue.text: Manage to convince, perhaps cuddling wife

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hold in the arms, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: say and perhaps both mean for example

explanation.surface: A husband hopes to win someone over by hugging his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To influence someone into agreeing is to win them round, which is what persuading successfully means.

clue.text: Rap session partially used for recess

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A chat session held in an alcove or during a break.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'used for recess' as the definition, but 'used for' is a link meaning 'gives'; only 'recess' can stand in for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess, typically at the end of a church.

clue.text: The Mousetrap benefitted from this extended ladder

parts.note: extended means long
a ladder in tights is a run

explanation.surface: A theatrical play is said to have profited from a stretched ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mousetrap is Agatha Christie's play, running in London's West End since 1952, the world's longest-running play.
explanation.definitionFit: A production staying on stage for many years has enjoyed a lengthy season of performances.

clue.text: Defeats political enforcers

definitions.meaning: to beat thoroughly, as in a sports thrashing
party officials who make MPs vote the party line

explanation.surface: Party disciplinarians are beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: informally to thrash an opponent, and the parliamentary officers who keep members voting with the party.

clue.text: Martial arts exponent's area that's protected

definitions.meaning: a grade of coloured sash held by a judo or karate student
land round a town where building is restricted

explanation.surface: A karate expert has a patch of ground that is safeguarded.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a green belt is countryside round a city where development is restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a coloured grade in martial arts; the other is a planning zone shielded from development.

clue.text: Family found in street with no money

indicators.note: one piece is discovered sitting inside the other

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A family turns up living on the street, penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is British slang for broke.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for broke or penniless.

clue.text: Staying power in a man — it's unusual!

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at the endurance one man shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the letters of A MAN IT'S; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance or the ability to keep going is a synonym of staying power.

clue.text: Lab working with kitchen solvent

indicators.note: letters put to work are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A laboratory uses a household cleaning fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Solvent in the financial sense: being in credit rather than in debt.

clue.text: Quietly showing discretion about one empty lorry holding up vessel

indicators.note: in a down answer the emptied lorry sits beneath the vessel, holding it up
the word for discretion goes round the numeral piece

parts.note: tact is discretion in dealing with others
I is the Roman numeral one
an urn is a vessel

indicators.note: an empty lorry has its middle cleared out, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: A driver quietly steers an empty truck carrying a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding up' suggests a container, but in a down entry it places the emptied lorry beneath the vessel as its support; 'about' and 'empty' work as usual, and 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying little and keeping silent, a reticent manner, is doing things quietly.

clue.text: Parish priests uncovered crime

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters are stripped away

parts.note: parsons are parish clergy

explanation.surface: Local clergymen are exposed as criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' removes the first and last letters of PARSONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: International clients in trouble must accept answer lacking flexibility

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take another letter in among them
the clients are in disarray, so their letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Clients of an international firm in difficulty find its responses rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges CLIENTS to give NELSTIC, and 'must accept' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable to stretch or bend, as with rigid material or fixed demand.

clue.text: Bad feeling, seeing the enemy number in here

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the word for here

parts.note: present means here, in attendance
time is called the enemy, as in the saying that time is the great enemy

explanation.surface: An uneasy feeling arises when the enemy turns up in numbers here.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreboding is a sense that something bad will happen.

clue.text: Amorous old criminal's rank

indicators.note: something criminal is bent, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: An elderly lecherous crook is in a low position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like a noun for status; here it is the adjective meaning foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Smelling foul or offensive; rank in its sense of stinking.

clue.text: Queen's supporting band (heavy metal) and will be instigator

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits below the others

parts.note: a ring is a band, as on a finger
lead is a heavy metal
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A queen backs a heavy metal band, and becomes its driving force.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who starts and leads a group in trouble or unrest is its instigator.

clue.text: Badmouthed missing leader and co-ordinated

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: maligned means spoken ill of

explanation.surface: A slandered person loses their leader and gets organised.
explanation.definitionFit: Lined up or brought into agreement, a synonym of co-ordinated.

clue.text: Entertainment on board could be playing cards with matches

parts.note: a deck is a pack of playing cards
matches are games, contests

explanation.surface: A shipboard pastime might be cards played alongside matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoits and shuffleboard are pastimes played on a ship's deck to amuse passengers.

clue.text: Show of hesitation by English dog trader

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow or tail them
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: An English dog dealer hesitates.
explanation.definitionFit: An online retailer is a merchant who sells over the internet.

clue.text: This slippery type left one alone finally going west

indicators.note: in an across answer going west means read right to left
finally takes the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: A slippery character finally left one person alone and headed west.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender snakelike fish notoriously hard to hold.

clue.text: Natural love must come before caring about …

indicators.note: the first piece is placed ahead of the second

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around and reordered

explanation.surface: Love naturally comes before caring, the clue suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CARING into RGANIC. The ellipsis joins this clue to the next one in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Produced without artificial chemicals, as in naturally farmed food.

clue.text: Officers with negative response from French company upset sergeant-major

parts.note: non is French for no

indicators.note: in a down answer upset turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

explanation.surface: A sergeant-major is annoyed by a refusal from a French company.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-commissioned officers such as corporals and sergeants; the informal plural for them.

clue.text: … characteristic of city pal needing reform

indicators.note: letters needing reform are reformed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A city friend in need of reform is typical, continuing the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Being representative of a kind, so showing its distinctive traits.

clue.text: 'Just use the oars', as said by some ruler once

indicators.note: as said means the words are heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: just means fair; to use the oars is to oar, to row

explanation.surface: A rower is told to simply row, in the words of an ancient ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the kings of ancient Egypt, rulers of long ago.

clue.text: The case for a two-day visit?

definitions.text: The case for a two-day visit?

parts.words: The case for a two-day visit?
parts.note: case suggests an argument for a short trip, but it is luggage packed for a single night away

explanation.surface: Someone argues the merits of a short stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A small holdall for a night away spans parts of two days.

clue.text: Projection from nine players given promotion

indicators.note: in a down answer promotion moves letters upward, so they read backwards

parts.note: a nonet is a group of nine musicians

explanation.surface: Nine team members are promoted to a protrusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue on a piece of wood made to fit a mortise joint is a projecting part.

clue.text: Crazy graduates needing to take time

indicators.note: the graduates must take the time letter inside them

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates

explanation.surface: Mad graduates need to take their time.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for mad, from having bats in the belfry.

clue.text: Black Sabbath's first shoots

parts.note: jet is a deep black colour

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: The rock band Black Sabbath's debut gets fired off.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurts of water or flame shot out under pressure.

clue.text: Casual worker of Bond villain and valet

parts.note: Oddjob is the henchman with the steel-rimmed hat in Goldfinger
a man, or manservant, is a valet

explanation.surface: A villain from a James Bond film and his manservant work part-time.
explanation.definitionFit: A handyman taking odd tasks as they come is a casual worker.

clue.text: Knowing of conflict within hospital department

indicators.note: the conflict word sits inside the department letters

parts.note: A and E is accident and emergency
war is conflict

explanation.surface: Someone is told of fighting breaking out in the emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscious of something, having knowledge of it.

clue.text: Emergency call about right types

indicators.note: the distress call goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: SOS is the Morse distress signal

explanation.surface: A distress call goes out regarding the right sort of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinds or varieties, as in all sorts of things.

clue.text: Dissertation on case of security and origin of nuclear fusion

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece written on another follows it
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters
origin means the opening letter

parts.note: a thesis is a dissertation

explanation.surface: A thesis about security cases and the beginnings of nuclear fusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Combining separate elements into a whole is a merging, or blending.
